holes.note: Meadow Gate: a gentle start through the valley meadows, before the climb
Twin Ridges: two fairways: the left ridge is shorter but a knife edge, the right valley is wide and long
The Spire: the green sits on a pinnacle of rock; miss it and you are on the scree, or worse
Cascade: a stream tumbles across the corner of the dogleg: carry it to cut the corner, or lay up short
Knife Edge: driveable along a ridge as narrow as a path, scree falling away on both sides
Eagle’s Nest: the green is out on a crag with a ravine all round: go for it in two over the drop, or lay up on the shelf to the right
Avalanche: from a tee high on the face, the ball flies forever; a scree fan waits on the right and a stream short of the green
Glassmere: all carry over a mountain tarn; the bail-out is right
Summit: the last of the climb, uphill all the way to the green below the summit lodge
Cloud Walk: driveable off the top, down a ridge into the clouds, scree either side all the way to the green
The Gorge: the stream cuts across the driving zone with a ravine down the left: a long carry, or lay up and go round
Falls View: downhill over a stream to a green with the falls beyond
Saddle: driveable: the green sits in a saddle between two tarns; lay up wide, or take them on
Rockfall: scree fields staggered down both sides of the fall line
High Road, Low Road: the high road is a narrow ridge on the left that shortens the hole; the low road on the right is safe and long
Hanging Green: a green on a ledge: the drop is right and long, scree on the left
Ravenhorn: the stream crosses the driving zone: lay up short, or carry it and leave a wedge
Homeward Falls: a closing par 5 to settle a match: the stream and its pool guard the green, the lay-up is out to the left
